sections.title: RAG: answering from your own data

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: No guide of yours covers this, so this page was written for the site, as of October 2026. Tools and versions change quickly: check the official documentation before relying on details.

blocks: A model doesn't know your documents. **Retrieval-augmented generation** finds relevant text and puts it in the prompt. This is the most common AI feature you'll be asked to build, and the most useful to practise.

blocks.title: The two RAG pipelines
blocks.code:
flowchart TD
  subgraph ingest[Ingestion, ahead of time]
    A[Documents] --> B[Split into chunks] --> C[Embed each chunk] --> D[(Vector store)]
  end
  subgraph query[Query, per request]
    Q[Question] --> E[Embed the question] --> F[Find similar chunks]
    D --> F
    F --> G[Prompt: rules, chunks, question] --> H[LLM] --> I[Answer with citations]
  end
blocks.caption: Retrieval quality limits answer quality: most bad RAG answers are retrieval problems.

sections.title: Embeddings and vector stores
blocks: An embedding model turns text into a vector so that similar meanings land close together. A vector store finds the nearest vectors, even when no words match. **You likely already run one:** PostgreSQL with the `pgvector` extension is a sensible first choice over a new database.

rows: A few hundred tokens with some overlap
Too large dilutes; too small loses context
More costs more and adds noise
Vector search misses exact codes and names
Security: never retrieve what the user can't see
blocks.caption: Starting values only: measure on your own data.

blocks.title: Ingest and ask
Good practice project
blocks.text: RAG over your own guides would make a strong portfolio project, because you can judge whether the answers are correct.

rows: Prompt allows it, or context is weak
Answer only from context; allow "I don't know"; add citations
Re-ingest on change, and track document versions
Filter by user permissions in the search itself

blocks.title: Interview angle
blocks.text: **Design a chatbot over company documents.** Cover ingestion and updates, chunking, embeddings, hybrid retrieval, access control at retrieval, the prompt with citations, streaming, evaluation, cost limits, and a fallback when nothing relevant is found.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- RAG: retrieve relevant text, then generate from it.
- Start with pgvector if you already use PostgreSQL.
- Enforce permissions during retrieval, never only in the prompt.
- Evaluate retrieval separately from generation.

items.question: Why not simply send all your documents to the model?
items.answer: They won't fit the context window, cost would be high, and irrelevant text reduces quality.

items.question: Vector search misses the error code `ERR-4021`. Why, and how do you fix it?
items.answer: Embeddings capture meaning and handle exact identifiers poorly. Add keyword search and combine the results.

items.question: Why isn't "don't reveal other tenants' data" in the prompt a security control?
items.answer: A prompt can be overridden or ignored. If a chunk isn't retrieved, it can't leak, so filter in the query.
